open_points.subject: Cabinet Kernel session ending
open_points.text: A09 does not include 'end an agent session' in Cabinet Kernel's operations, while A11 says 'Cabinet Kernel ends a session when its agent session ends'.
open_points.question: Is Cabinet Kernel authorized to end an agent session, despite that operation being absent from its A09 rights row?
options: Add ending a session to Kernel's authorized operations
Only the owner may end sessions
Treat ending as part of another listed Kernel operation
open_points.default_guess: Authorize Cabinet Kernel to end sessions.

open_points.subject: agent-authority refusal precedence
open_points.text: A10 requires indistinguishable not-found answers for an ungranted or nonexistent project, but does not order that check against request validation, type validation, archived-state checks or replay checks.
open_points.question: Which refusal wins when an agent-authority call fails both the session/project access check and another validation?
options: Authenticate and check session/grant before all operation-specific validation
Validate the request before checking the grant
Define a per-operation precedence
open_points.default_guess: Check token, registered session and project grant first, then perform operation-specific validation.

open_points.subject: pointer operations under agent authority
open_points.text: A10 applies the third check 'for an operation on a project', while withdrawal is defined by an artifact pointer and the texts do not say whether the request also names its project or when Registry resolves the pointer's project.
open_points.question: How is the session's project-set check performed for withdrawal or another operation whose direct identifier is a pointer rather than a project?
options: Require both project id and pointer id and check their association
Resolve the pointer internally and check its project
Treat the pointer lookup as occurring before the access check
open_points.default_guess: Resolve the pointer without disclosing it, check its project against the session, and return the same not-found refusal on failure.

open_points.subject: access-version increment
open_points.text: A12 says the version 'moves by one with each accepted change of its granted set, its active project or its pending request', while one action can change several of those facts together.
open_points.question: Does one accepted action increment the access version once, or once for every access fact it changes?
options: Once per accepted action
Once per changed fact
Define increments separately for each compound action
open_points.default_guess: Increment once per accepted action that changes any session-access fact.

open_points.subject: owner-session idle activity
open_points.text: A13 ends a session after '30 minutes without an owner action' but does not define whether reads, refused actions, confirmation-page views or only accepted changes count, nor how last_action is initialized.
open_points.question: Which requests refresh the owner session's inactivity deadline?
options: Every authenticated owner-interface request
Only successfully accepted owner actions, including reads
Only accepted state-changing actions
open_points.default_guess: Initialize last_action at sign-in and refresh it on every successfully authenticated owner-interface request.

open_points.subject: sign-in lockout window
open_points.text: A13 says that after five refused sign-ins, 'every sign-in ... is refused for the next 15 minutes', without saying whether refusals during lockout extend or restart it, whether the counter survives restart, or how simultaneous attempts are counted.
open_points.question: What are the exact counter, lockout and reset semantics for sign-in throttling?
options: A fixed 15-minute lock beginning at the fifth refusal; lockout refusals do not extend it
A sliding lock extended by every refused attempt
Clear the counter on restart
Persist the counter and lock across restart
open_points.default_guess: Use an atomic instance-wide counter, start a fixed 15-minute lock at the fifth refusal, do not extend it with locked attempts, and keep it only in runtime state.

open_points.subject: confirmation-step lifetime
open_points.text: A13 says a confirmation step is 'valid only in the session that showed it, and once' but gives no expiry, invalidation rule after intervening state changes, or definition of what state makes it single-use.
open_points.question: Until when is a shown confirmation valid, and what invalidates or consumes it?
options: Until the owner session ends, consumed by the first submission attempt
Until the owner session ends, consumed only by an accepted action
Short independent expiry with operation-specific state revalidation
open_points.default_guess: Keep it valid until the owner session ends, consume it on the first submission attempt, and recheck all action preconditions at submission.

open_points.subject: concurrent publish replay
open_points.text: A07 says of two concurrent publishes that 'both are accepted with consecutive versions', while A01 says two calls with the same publish request id make only one pointer.
open_points.question: Does A07's two-publish rule apply only when the calls carry different request ids?
options: Yes, identical request ids collapse to one publish
No, all concurrent calls create consecutive versions
Define a separate outcome for simultaneous identical request ids
open_points.default_guess: Apply consecutive versions only to distinct request ids; simultaneous repeats return the same pointer.

open_points.subject: publish-withdraw concurrency
open_points.text: A07 serialises 'Publishes of one type on one project' but gives no ordering rule for a publish racing a withdrawal of the currently published pointer.
open_points.question: What outcomes are allowed when publication and withdrawal of the same project's type occur concurrently?
options: Serialize both operations on the project-and-type key
Allow either transaction order with the corresponding success or refusal
Give publication precedence
Give withdrawal precedence
open_points.default_guess: Serialize both on the project-and-type key and allow either lock-acquisition order.

open_points.subject: removed artifact type in projections
open_points.text: A22 says pointers of a removed type 'are listed and read as before', but also says latest-by-type is refused, and it does not say whether a still-published pointer of that type remains in the agent projection's current pointers.
open_points.question: Which read projections continue to expose pointers of a removed type?
options: Artifact history and agent projection still expose them; latest-by-type alone is refused
Only artifact history lists them
All generic projections omit them after removal
open_points.default_guess: Keep them in artifact history and in any generic current-pointer projection, while refusing the type-specific latest operation.

open_points.subject: re-adding an artifact type
open_points.text: A22 defines adding and removing types but does not say what happens if a later release declares the same type name again after removal.
open_points.question: Does re-adding the same type resume its existing version history and published pointer, or create a logically new vocabulary entry?
options: Resume the existing history and continue its versions
Forbid reusing a removed type name
Treat it as a new type with a new identity or name
open_points.default_guess: Forbid reusing a removed type name unless a later decision explicitly defines migration semantics.

open_points.subject: audit erasure date
open_points.text: A15 refuses a date 'later than today' and uses the UTC start of the supplied date, but does not define which timezone determines 'today'.
open_points.question: Is 'today' the current UTC date or the owner's local date?
options: UTC date
Owner-interface configured timezone
Europe/Madrid local date
open_points.default_guess: Use the current UTC date, matching the stated UTC cutoff.

open_points.subject: import mapping contents
open_points.text: A16 says the mapping shows each project 'with its id, status, rooms and pointers' and Customers the import will make, but does not state which facts of rooms, pointers, objects and customers are shown.
open_points.question: What exact information must the owner see before confirming that the mapping is the one to apply?
options: Every imported fact and every old-to-new customer link
Only identities, statuses and link summaries
A State 6 answer shape may choose the displayed subset
open_points.default_guess: Show every value that will be stored or discarded, every identity, and every old-to-new link.

open_points.subject: v1 customer mapping inputs
open_points.text: M04 requires the owner to give each imported Customer its kind and name and to say whether the old v1 customer reference is its tax id, while A16 does not say that the mapping collects or displays those decisions.
open_points.question: Must the import mapping require and confirm the Customer name, kind and old-reference-to-tax-id decision for every new Customer?
options: Yes, all are mandatory mapping inputs
Only name and kind are mandatory; tax-id treatment defaults to discarded
The import file supplies them
open_points.default_guess: Require and display all three decisions in the confirmed mapping.

open_points.subject: unpicked import records
open_points.text: A16 shows every record and says 'Any conflict ... a malformed record' refuses the whole import, while the transaction stores only the projects the owner picked.
open_points.question: Do conflicts or malformed records belonging only to unpicked projects refuse the import?
options: Validate and reject the entire file
Validate only the selected projects and their transitive records
Reject malformed file structure globally but ignore record conflicts outside the selected closure
open_points.default_guess: Validate file structure globally, but apply identity and domain checks only to selected projects and the records they require.

open_points.subject: malformed import record
open_points.text: A16 lists 'a malformed record' as a whole-import refusal without defining semantic malformation beyond production id conflicts.
open_points.question: Which internal inconsistencies make an import record malformed?
options: Only violations of the State 6 file schema
Also duplicate ids within the file, dangling links, invalid pointer histories, invalid statuses and nonconsecutive versions
Define a separate exhaustive import-integrity rule
open_points.default_guess: Reject schema violations and every violation of the accepted model invariants, including duplicates, dangling links and invalid pointer histories.

open_points.subject: import file digest
open_points.text: A16 binds mapping, confirmation, closure and audit to 'the file's digest' but specifies neither the digest algorithm nor whether it covers the original bytes or a canonicalized representation.
open_points.question: How is the import file digest computed?
options: A fixed cryptographic digest of the exact uploaded bytes
A digest of a canonical parsed representation
Leave the algorithm and representation to State 6
open_points.default_guess: Use a release-fixed cryptographic digest of the exact uploaded bytes.

open_points.subject: secret randomness
open_points.text: A17 requires every secret to be 'generated at random by the owner's vault', but Registry receives only the resulting value and cannot verify its origin or entropy.
open_points.question: Is vault generation an external operational requirement, or must Registry verify some measurable property beyond byte length and inequality?
options: Treat generation as an external owner obligation and verify only length and inequality
Require an encoded format carrying generation metadata
Apply a heuristic strength check
open_points.default_guess: Treat random vault generation as external and have Registry verify only the stated observable properties.

open_points.subject: daily backup schedule and retention
open_points.text: A18 says backups occur 'once a day', are 'kept 30 days', and no erased value remains after t + 30 days, but gives no scheduling boundary or deletion deadline.
open_points.question: What exact cadence and deletion rule satisfy the daily and 30-day requirements?
options: One backup per UTC calendar day and delete at exact age 30 days
At most 24 hours between successful backups and purge all backups older than 30 days
One backup per owner-local calendar day with a daily purge
open_points.default_guess: Require no more than 24 hours between successful backups and delete each backup no later than its creation instant plus 30 days.

open_points.subject: production restore-test instance
open_points.text: A18 requires restoring a production backup 'into a temporary instance on VM Platform' and then says 'a test instance never receives a production backup', while State 0 defines any non-production instance as a test instance with no production personal data.
open_points.question: Is the temporary restore instance an allowed exception to the rule that test instances receive no production data?
options: Create an explicit isolated restore-test exception
Do not use production backups for release restore tests
Treat the temporary restore as part of production rather than another instance
open_points.default_guess: Define a tightly isolated temporary production-restore environment as an explicit exception, accessible only to the owner and destroyed after the test.

open_points.subject: reapplying erasures after restore
open_points.text: A18 requires the owner to 'repeat every erasure made after the backup's instant' before serving, but does not say how those erasures are identified or how revision checks, confirmations, no-ops and dependent session changes are handled during replay.
open_points.question: What durable source and replay semantics guarantee that every post-backup erasure is reapplied correctly before service resumes?
options: Use an external governance ledger with a defined privileged recovery replay
Replay ordinary owner operations with their normal revision and confirmation checks
Use a Registry-maintained erasure journal outside the backed-up store
open_points.default_guess: Use an external, durable erasure ledger and a defined recovery procedure that reapplies the resulting state without ordinary stale-revision failures.

open_points.subject: release restore-test acceptance
open_points.text: A18 says the restored instance is checked to ensure that it 'starts and answers' without defining which answer, integrity checks or failure condition block the release.
open_points.question: What constitutes a successful restore test at release time?
options: Startup plus one health response
Startup plus model-integrity checks and representative authenticated reads
A complete required restore-test suite declared by the release
open_points.default_guess: Require a release-declared restore suite covering startup, store integrity and representative authenticated reads.

open_points.subject: dependency scope
open_points.text: A20 requires a release to name 'every dependency it runs with' by exact version and digest but does not define whether this includes transitive packages, the language runtime, system libraries, database engine or operating-system components.
open_points.question: What artifacts are members of release.dependencies?
options: Direct application packages only
All direct and transitive language packages
Every executable and library in the deployable image, including runtime and system packages
open_points.default_guess: Cover every direct and transitive component shipped in the deployable image; treat host firmware and hypervisor as outside the Registry release.

open_points.subject: security-review completeness
open_points.text: A21 says 'Every security category has exactly one outcome below' but declares no authoritative universe of security categories against which completeness can be checked.
open_points.question: What fixed catalogue determines whether the security review includes every required category?
options: The nine categories listed in A21 are themselves the complete catalogue
Reference a separately versioned security-review catalogue
Allow reviewers to add categories without reopening the decision
open_points.default_guess: Declare the nine listed category identifiers to be the complete, versioned catalogue for this review.

open_points.subject: create replay comparison state
open_points.text: A01 compares a repeated create with the original 'supplied facts', but M01, M03, M04 and M05 keep only the request id, not an immutable copy of those original facts; project and customer facts can later be corrected.
open_points.question: Against which values is a replay compared after the created record has changed?
options: Store an immutable creation-facts fingerprint or snapshot
Compare against the record's current facts
Accept every reuse of the request id regardless of supplied facts
open_points.default_guess: Store an immutable canonical snapshot or fingerprint of the original supplied facts.

open_points.subject: blank optional values in replay comparison
open_points.text: A01 compares supplied facts 'as the caller gave them', while A02 treats an optional empty or whitespace-only string as absent.
open_points.question: Are an omitted optional value and a supplied blank optional value equal for request-id replay?
options: Equal after A02 converts both to absent
Different because A01 compares raw caller input
Store both raw and effective forms
open_points.default_guess: Compare the effective supplied facts after A02's blank-to-absent rule.

open_points.subject: create replay check precedence
open_points.text: A01 expressly puts authorization and archived-project checks before a publish replay, but gives no corresponding rule for project, customer, room or other create replays.
open_points.question: Does a valid replay return its existing record before current parent and domain preconditions are checked, such as an add-room replay after its project was archived?
options: Replay lookup and equality take precedence after authentication
All current operation preconditions take precedence
Define precedence separately for each create operation
open_points.default_guess: After authentication and authority checks, return an equal replay before rechecking mutable domain preconditions, except where a rule explicitly says otherwise.

open_points.subject: blank-value character set
open_points.text: A02 defines blank as 'white space only' and formalizes it with strip(v), whose recognized characters differ across languages and libraries.
open_points.question: Which Unicode characters count as whitespace for the required-value and optional-value rules?
options: ASCII whitespace only
Unicode White_Space property
The implementation language's default strip behavior
open_points.default_guess: Use the Unicode White_Space property fixed to the Unicode version of the release.

open_points.subject: repeat grant or activation of an archived project
open_points.text: A05 accepts granting a project already in the set and making the active project active again as no-ops, while R0-70 says an archived project cannot be granted or made active; a project may become archived while still granted and active.
open_points.question: If an archived project is already granted or active, is repeating that grant or activation accepted as a no-op or refused because the project is archived?
options: No-op detection takes precedence and it is accepted
The archived-project refusal takes precedence
Grant is accepted as a no-op but activation is refused
open_points.default_guess: Apply the archived-project refusal before no-op handling for both operations.

open_points.subject: list sort directions
open_points.text: A06 says lists are 'by' names or identities but specifies direction only for latest/highest/earliest and audit sequence; it does not explicitly give ascending or descending direction for the remaining keys and tie-breakers.
open_points.question: What direction applies to every unnamed sort key and identity tie-breaker?
options: All unspecified keys are ascending
All tie-breakers are ascending but primary keys vary by list
Declare every key's direction separately
open_points.default_guess: Treat every key without an explicit direction as ascending.
